carla_support: FYI — customer reported a spike of errors on embeddings endpoint (POST /v1/embeddings). Multiple 400s with a 'dimension mismatch' message, plus elevated latency reported. Started a ticket: TKT-4821.

mira_oncall: Thanks Carla. Any request samples or logs? Which model?

carla_support: Pasted the minimal failing payload from customer (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-fa-sim-v1",
  "input": [[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ... up to 1024 floats]]
}
```

Error returned: `400 Bad Request - Dimension mismatch: expected 768, got 1024`. Customer says they used this payload for weeks and nothing changed on their side.

sam_ml: That error means the model backend is expecting a 768-dim vector for the provided model id. Two possibilities: model binary updated (new embedding size) or routing sent request to wrong model variant.

alex_sre: I'm seeing a pattern in metrics: increased 4xxs on /embeddings around 09:14 UTC, and small bump in 5xxs approx 09:18. Throughput on embedding-serving cluster E-1 is normal, but a subset of nodes returned the mismatch. Could be a bad rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: refs/heads/main @ commit a1b2c3d (09:05 UTC).

mira_oncall: @sam_ml can you check model registry and deployment history for embed-fa-sim-v1 around that commit?

sam_ml: Looking... model config shows embed-fa-sim-v1 has two variants: v1.0 (768) and v1.1 (1024). We recently added v1.1 for experimental dense model. The routing table should map customers on older contract to v1.0, but a config change earlier today may have flipped the default alias to v1.1.

carla_support: Customer is on hosted API (no pinned version). They expect the older 768 dims. They started seeing errors exactly after the 09:05 deploy.

alex_sre: Confirmed: there's a config entry change in feature-flags service at 09:06 that updated alias `embed-fa-sim` -> `embed-fa-sim:v1.1`. Some workers pulled updated alias before model binaries were available on all clusters — leads to routing to v1.1 on nodes that didn't have the model loaded, causing dimension mismatch when the request body contained older vector sizes.

mira_oncall: This is a partial outage / bad rollout. Immediate mitigation: rollback alias to v1.0 and scale a warm-up job to prefetch v1.1 binaries to other pools.

alex_sre: Rolling back alias now...

deploy-bot: Rollback action: alias embed-fa-sim -> embed-fa-sim:v1.0 by alex_sre (09:29 UTC).

ops-bot: Alert resolved? Alias change detected, propagation to routing layer will take ~30s.

sam_ml: Also adding temporary validation in the router: reject embedding requests where the request vector length doesn't match the resolved model dims with a clearer message linking to docs. That will avoid silent misrouting behavior.

john_custsuccess: I've told the customer we're rolling back the alias and will follow up with root cause. They were seeing ~15% of their requests fail and latency for some requests doubled during retries. They asked for any quota credits.

mira_oncall: Good. After rollback, error rate on embeddings dropped back to baseline within ~90s. I can confirm from logs: 4xx went down from 12% -> 0.8%. 5xx spike subsided.

alex_sre: Postmortem actions: 1) Add pre-deploy validation ensuring alias changes are accompanied by model availability across target clusters. 2) Introduce a canary window before alias flip for global aliases. 3) Add a router-level safeguard: if model dims don't match request, return structured error with model alias & expected dims.

sam_ml: I'll coordinate the model registry change: mark v1.1 as 'not-ready' until binaries are synced and add a graph check that blocks alias promotion if any cluster reports missing binaries.

carla_support: Customer wants ETA on credits. Ops: please route to billing for 1) incident credit and 2) manual retry guidance.

mira_oncall: Quick repro steps for internal ticket: 1) Craft an embedding request with vector length 1024 to alias `embed-fa-sim` while alias points to v1.0 -> should 400 with explicit mismatch. 2) Flip alias to v1.1 while only subset of nodes have v1.1 loaded -> some requests succeed, some 400. 3) Observe router logs: mismatch + routing decisions.

alex_sre: Extra notes on batching/throughput: customers sending large batch inputs (N>64) were more likely to hit edge nodes with mismatched variants because of cross-shard routing. We'll add a note to Optimize recommending smaller batches during canary windows.

sam_ml: I'm pushing a quick router patch to add explicit dim-check for the next hour, will alert when prod patch is live.

mira_oncall: Thanks team. Status: mitigated (alias rollback). Open follow-ups: SRE-312 (pre-deploy validation), ML-451 (registry sync checks), DOCS-98 (error message documentation), and Billing ticket. I'll file incident stub.

carla_support: Customer updated: appreciates quick fix, asked for postmortem. Leaving them a contact.

mira_oncall: Closing loop here in 24h after follow-ups done. If anyone sees a reoccur, re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
